G8324.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to draw up, furl  sails, (Odyssey by Homer): to draw up  cables, etc., [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—; κρόκα ἐν στήμονι μηρύσασθαι to weave  the woof into the warp, (Hesiod) 
3. Pass., κισσὸς μαρύεται περὶ χείλη ivy winds  round the edge, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8326.definition:
1. = Lat. machina: 
2. an instrument, machine  for lifting weights and the like, (Herdotus Historicus); μ. Ποσειδῶνος, of the trident, (Aeschulus Tragicus); λαοπόροις μ., of Xerxes' bridge of boats, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. an engine  of war, (Thucydides) 
4. a theatrical machine , by which gods were made to appear in the air, (Plato Philosophus): hence proverbial of any sudden appearance, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ μηχανῆς (cf. Lat. deus ex machina), (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. any contrivance , for doing a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: in plural μηχαναί, shifts, devices, arts, wiles , (Hesiod), attic; μηχαναῖς Διός by the arts  of Zeus, (Aeschulus Tragicus); proverbial, μηχαναὶ Σισύφου (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Phrases, μηχανήν or μηχανὰς προσφέρειν (Euripides); εὑρίσκειν (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;with genitive, μ. κακῶν a contrivance against  ills, (Euripides); but, μ. σωτηρίας a way of providing  safety, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. οὐδεμία μηχανή [ ἐστι] ὅπως οὐ, with future, (Herdotus Historicus); also, μὴ οὐ, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. in adverb, phrases, ἐκ μηχανῆς τινος in some way  or other, (Herdotus Historicus); μηδεμιῆι μηχανῆι by no means  whatsoever, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8329.definition: red chalk, ruddle , Lat. rubrica, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8332.definition:
1. hate, hatred : and so, 
2. passive hate borne  one, a being hated , [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. active hate felt against  another, a grudge , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; μ. τινός τινι felt by  one against  another, (Euripides) 
4. of persons, a hateful object , = μίσημα, [variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G8333.definition:
1. a belt  or girdle , worn round the waist beneath  the cuirass (whereas the ζωστήρ went over  it), (Iliad by Homer) 
2. = ζώνη, the maiden-zone , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), etc. 
3. a girdle worn by wrestlers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. a head-band  worn by Greek women to tie up their hair, a snood , (Euripides) 
5. the victor's chaplet  at the games, (Pindar); Λυδία μίτρα a Lydian garland  (i. e. an ode in Lydian measure), (Pindar) 
6. a Persian head-dress, turban , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8335.definition:
1. to remember wrongs done one, remember past injuries , (Herdotus Historicus); οὐ μν. to bear  no malice, pass an act of amnesty , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: with dative pers. et genitive rei, μ. τινί τινος to bear  one a grudge for  a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. with accusative rei, τὴν ἡλικίαν μν. to remind  one of the ills  of age, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8341.definition:
1. staying in one's place, stable, steadfast , (Sophocles Tragicus); of soldiers, Lat. statarius, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. of things, conditions and the like, abiding, lasting, stable , Lat. stabilis, (Euripides), etc. (ML)

G8345.definition: to fight in single combat , (Euripides); τινι with one, (Herdotus Historicus); of the Athenians at Marathon, μοῦνοι μουνομαχήσαντες τῷ Πέρσῃ having fought single-handed  with the Persians, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8351.definition:
1. to be weary with toil, to be sore distressed , (Iliad by Homer):—; to work hard, labour , (Euripides), etc.; with accusative cognate, μ. μόχθους, πόνους to undergo  hardships, or to execute painful  tasks, (Euripides); μ. μαθήματα to toil at  learning, (Euripides) 
2. with accusative objecti, τέκνα ἁμόχθησα the children whom I toiled for, (Euripides); μ. τινά θεραπεύμασιν = θεραπεύειν, (Euripides); compare μόχθος. (ML)

G8352.definition:
1. a bar  used as a lever, a crowbar, handspike , Lat, vectis , used for moving ships, (Odyssey by Homer); for forcing doors and gates, (Euripides) 
2. the stake  which Ulysses ran into the Cyclops' eye, (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. a wooden bar , placed across gates on the inside and secured by the βάλανος, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8353.definition: the shrew-mouse, field-mouse , Lat. mus araneus, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8355.definition: a fly , Lat. musca, (Iliad by Homer):—;proverbial, μυίης θάρσος, of excessive boldness, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8356.definition:
1. the nose, snout , (Aristophanes Comicus): in plural the nostrils , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. from the use of the nose to express ridicule, a sneerer , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8358.definition:
1. Lat. mola, a mill, a handmill turned by women, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. the nether millstone , (Aristophanes Comicus); the upper being ὄνος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8362.definition: 0, 000  times as many as , with genitive, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8365.definition:
1. Lat. formica, the ant, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. a beast of prey  in India, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8366.definition:
1. = μύρτος, (Pindar) 
2. a branch  or wreath of myrtle , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8367.definition:
1. Lat. mus, a mouse, (Batrachomyomachia); μ. ἀρουραῖος the field-mouse , or the hamster , (Herdotus Historicus); μῦς πίσσας γεύεται, proverbial of one who is tempted to eat and finds himself caught, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. a muscle  of the body, Lat. musculus, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8368.definition:
1. foul, dirty : hence, loathsome, abominable , (Euripides); τὸ μ. an abomination , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of persons, defiled, polluted , (Euripides) (ML)

G8369.definition: doric and Lacon. word, the upper lip, the moustache , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): compare μάσταξ. (ML)

G8374.definition: anything flowing, running water, a river, stream , [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8375.definition: a wooded vale, dell , or glen , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8376.definition:
to grow stiff  or numb , Lat. torpere, (Iliad by Homer) 
from νάρκη (ML)

G8378.definition:
1. seafaring, naval , ὁ ν. στρατός opposite to ὁ πεζός, (Herdotus Historicus); ν. λεώς (Aeschulus Tragicus); στόλος (Sophocles Tragicus); ν. ἐρείπια wrecks of ships , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ν. ἀναρχία among the seamen , (Euripides):—; τὸ ναυτικόν a navy, fleet , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. of persons, skilled in seamanship, nautical , ναυτικοὶ ἐγένοντο became a naval power , (Thucydides) 
3. ἡ ναυτική (i.e. τέχνη); navigation, seamanship , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὰ ναυτικά (Plato Philosophus);—;but, τὰ ναυτικά, also, naval affairs naval power , (Thucydides) 
4. at Athens, ναυτικόν technically meant money borrowed  or lent on bottomry , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8379.definition:
1. a young woman, girl, maiden , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. as adjective youthful , (Euripides) 
3. new , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8381.definition: the young of the deer, a fawn , (Homer), etc.; πέδιλα νεβρῶν fawnskin  brogues, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8384.definition:
1. a quarrel, wrangle, strife , (Homer), etc. 
2. strife of words, railing, abuse, a taunt, reproach , (Iliad by Homer) 
3. a strife at law, dispute before a judge , (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. battle, fight , (Homer); ν. φυλόπιδος (Odyssey by Homer); of dissensions between whole nations , νεῖκος πρὸς Καρχηδονίους (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. cause of strife, matter of quarrel , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8385.definition:
1. to deal out, distribute, dispense , of meat and drink, (Homer), etc.; of the gods, νέμει ὄλβον Ὀλύμπιος ἀνθρώποισιν (Odyssey by Homer); μοῖραν ν. τινί to pay  one due  respect, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass., ἐπὶ τοὺς Ἕλληνας νέμεται is freely bestowed  upon them, (Herdotus Historicus); κρέα νενεμημένα portions  of meat, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. Mid. to distribute among themselves , and so, to have as one's portion, possess, enjoy , (Homer), etc. 
3. to dwell in, inhabit , (Homer): absolute to dwell , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. to spend, pass , αἰῶνα, ἡμέραν (Pindar) 
5. Act. much like Mid. to hold, possess , γῆν, χώραν, πόλιν (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass., of places, to be inhabited , (Herdotus Historicus); of a country, to maintain itself, be constituted , (Thucydides) 
6. to hold sway, manage , (Herdotus Historicus):—; ν. οἴακα to manage  the helm, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ν. ἰσχὺν ἐπὶ σκήπτροισι to support  one's strength on staves, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ν. γλῶσσαν to use  the tongue, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. like νομίζω, to hold, consider as  so and so, σὲ νέμω θεόν (Sophocles Tragicus); προστάτην ν. τινά to take  as one's patron, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
8. of herdsmen, to pasture  or graze  their flocks, drive to pasture, tend , Lat. pascere, (Odyssey by Homer), attic, etc.:—;metaphorically, ν. χόλον (Sophocles Tragicus) 
9. Mid., of cattle, to feed , i. e. go to pasture, graze , Lat. pasci, (Homer), etc.: with accusative cognate to feed on , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; of men, to eat , (Sophocles Tragicus); of fire, to consume, devour , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; of cancerous sores, to spread , ἐνέμετο πρόσω (Herdotus Historicus) 
10. with accusative loci, ὄρη νέμειν to graze  the hills [with cattle, 5th/4th c.BC]: Pass., [ τὸ ὄρος] νέμεται βουσί (Xenophon Historicus) 
11. metaphorically, πυρὶ νέμειν πόλιν to give  a city to the flames, (Herdotus Historicus): Pass., πυρὶ χθὼν νέμεται the land is devoured  by fire, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8386.definition: to renovate, renew , νέωσον (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Mid., τάφους ἐνεώσατο had  them renewed , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8388.definition: a nod  or sign , (Thucydides); νεύματος ἕνεκα for a mere nod , i. e. without cause , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8389.definition: a string  or cord of sinew, a bowstring , (Homer), etc. (ML)

G8391.definition:
1. a sinew, tendon;  in plural, the tendons of the feet , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. metaphorically in plural, τὰ νεῦρα τῆς τραγῳδίας, of lyric odes, their sinews, vigour , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ νεῦρα τῶν πραγμάτων (Aeschines Orator) 
3. gut, cord made of sinew , for fastening the head of the arrow to the shaft, (Iliad by Homer): the cord of a sling , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8398.definition:
in (Herdotus Historicus) and attic λίτρον, carbonate of soda , (Herdotus Historicus) 
Prob. a foreign word. (ML)

G8400.definition:
1. thoughtful, intelligent , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. in one's right mind , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8402.definition:
1. roaming about for pasture : οἱ Νομάδες roaming, pastoral tribes, Nomads , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; and as proper noun, Numidians , (Polybius Historicus) 
2. feminine adjective grazing, feeding, at pasture , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. metaphorically, κρῆναι νομάδες wandering  streams, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8403.definition:
1. conformable to custom, usage , or law, customary, prescriptive, established, lawful, rightful , (Euripides):—; νόμιμόν [ ἐστί] τινι ποιεῖν τι (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. νόμιμα, ων, τά, usages, customs , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
3. funeral rites , Lat. justa, (Thucydides) 
4. adverb -μως, (Plato Philosophus): comparative -ώτερον (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8405.definition:
1. a feeding-place  for cattle, pasture , (Homer); ν. ὕλης a woodland pasture , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. herbage , (Homeric Hymns):—;generally, food , (Hesiod) 
3. metaphorically, ἐπέων πολὺς νομός a wide range  for words, (Iliad by Homer) 
4. an abode allotted  or assigned  to one, a district, province , (Pindar), etc.; νομὸν ἔχειν to have one's dwelling-place , (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. one of the districts  into which Egypt was divided, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; applied also to other provinces , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8406.definition: ν. κοίτη a bed of sickness , (Euripides):—;adverb, νοσερῶς ἔχειν τὸ σῶμα (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8409.definition: carrying on the back : as Substantive a beast of burthen , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8410.definition: admonition, warning , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; τἀμὰ νουθετήματα given to me, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8412.definition: by night, nightly , Lat. nocturnus, (Aristophanes Comicus); ν. γενέσθαι to happen by night , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8413.definition: a bat , Lat. vespertilio, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8422.definition: to make yellow  or brown , by roasting or frying, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8423.definition:
1. belonging to a friend and guest, hospitable , Ζεὺς ξένιος as protector of the rights of hospitality , (Iliad by Homer):—; τράπεζα ξ. the guests'  table, (Odyssey by Homer); ξένιός τινι bound  to him by ties of hospitality , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. ξείνια, attic ξένια, ων, τά, friendly gifts, meat and drink , given to the guest by his host, (Homer); ξένια παρέσχε δαῖτα as a friendly gift , (Aeschulus Tragicus); βοῦν ξένια ἔπεμψεν (Xenophon Historicus); ἐπὶ ξένια καλεῖν to invite any one to eat with you , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; metaphorically, θάνατος ξένιά σοι γενήσεται (Euripides) 
3. foreign , (Pindar), attic (ML)

G8426.definition: a sword , (Homer); distinguished from μάχαιρα, q. see. (ML)

G8434.definition: a rasor , (Homer), etc.:—;proverb, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς ὄλεθρος ἠὲ βιῶναι death or life is balanced on a rasor's  edge, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπὶ ξυροῦ τῆς ἀκμῆς ἔχεται ἡμῖν τὰ πράγματα (Herdotus Historicus); βεβὼς ἐπὶ ξυρῷ τύχης (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8436.definition:
1. to scrape, plane, smooth  or polish , (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, ξῦσαι ἀπὸ γῆρας to scrape off, get rid of  old age, (Homeric Hymns):—; Mid., παλτὸν ξύσασθαι to shape oneself  a javelin-shaft, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to make smooth, work delicately , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8437.definition:
1. a small spit , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. a coin stamped with a spit , (Plutarch) 
3. the leg of a compass , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8438.definition: an obol , as a weight, = 1/6th part of a δραχμή, worth rather more than three halfpence, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐν δυοῖν ὀβολοῖν θεωρεῖν, as we might say "to sit in the shilling gallery, " (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8444.definition: a wayfarer, traveller , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;in (Iliad by Homer), a fellow-traveller , or guide.  (ML)

G8445.definition:
1. to make  or level a road , (Xenophon Historicus):—; Pass., of roads, to be made fit for use , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. metaphorically to reduce to a system , τι (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. with dative pers. to act as pioneer, serve as guide , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to make one's way, advance , Lat. progredi, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8447.definition:
1. to lament, bewail, mourn for : 
2. with accusative pers., (Homer); with accusative rei, ὁ δ᾽ ὀδύρετο πατρίδα γαῖαν mourned for  it, i. e. for the want of it, (Odyssey by Homer); so, νόστον ὀδυρομένη (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. with genitive pers. to mourn for, for the sake of , (Homer) 
4. with dative pers. to wail  or lament to  or before  others, (Homer) 
5. absolute to wail, mourn , (Homer) (ML)

G8448.definition: to steer , and so to guide, manage , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8449.definition:
1. kindred, relationship , (Herdotus Historicus), attic: intimacy, friendliness, kindness , (Thucydides):—;in plural friendly relations , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. of words, the proper sense , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8450.definition:
1. feminine of οἰκέτης, (Euripides) 
2. the mistress of the house , Lat. matrona, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8451.definition:
1. the act of dwelling, habitation , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2. management, administration , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. a house, dwelling, residence , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; κατασκαφὴς οἴκ. of the grave, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8453.definition:
1. an inhabitant , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἰκ. θεοῦ one who dwells  in the temple of the god, (Euripides); Ἅιδου οἰκ., of one dead, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. a colonist , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8454.definition:
1. with accusative rei, to found as a colony  or new settlement , πόλιν (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; Pass., πόλις οἴκισται (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to people  with new settlers, colonise , χώρην (Herdotus Historicus); νήσους (Thucydides):—;Mid. ὅπη γῆς πύργον οἰκιούμεθα in what part of the world we shall make ourselves  a fenced home, (Euripides) 
3. with accusative pers. to remove, transplant , (Euripides); metaphorically, τὸν μὲν ἀφ᾽ ὑψηλῶν βραχὺν ὤικισεν brought  him from high to low estate, (Euripides):—;Pass. to settle  in a place, (Euripides) (ML)

G8456.definition: born in the house, homebred , of slaves, Lat. verna, (Plato Philosophus); of quails, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8457.definition:
1. the site of a house , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
2. the house itself, a building , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8459.definition:
pity, compassion , (Odyssey by Homer), Dht., attic:—;with genitive objecti, compassion for , οἶκτος τῆς πόλιος (Herdotus Historicus) 
 the expression of pity, lamentation, piteous wailing , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;and in plural, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8460.definition:
1. pitiable, in piteous plight , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. of things, pitiable, piteous, lamentable , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
3. in active sense, piteous , (Odyssey by Homer); οἰκτρᾶς γόον ὄρνιθος, of the nightingale, (Sophocles Tragicus);—;neuter plural as regularly adverb οἰκτρῶς, (Aeschulus Tragicus) —;Besides comparative and Sup. οἰκτρότερος, -τατος, (Homer) has an irreg. Sup. οἴκτιστος (q. see.). (ML)

G8461.definition:
exclamation of pain, fright, pity, anger, grief, also of surprise, properly οἴ μοι ah me! woe's me!  (Theognis Elegiacus);—;with genitive causae, οἴμοι τῶν κακῶν, οἴμοι γέλωτος ah me  for my misfortunes, for the laughter, [variant datesTragica Adespota 
The last syllable in οἴμοι may be elided before ὡς. (ML)

G8464.definition: a can for ladling wine  from the mixing bowl  κρατήρ); into the cups, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8466.definition:
1. to intoxicate , οἰνῶσαι σῶμα ποτοῖς (Critias Philosophus) 
2. Pass. οἰνόομαι to get drunk, be drunken , οἰνωθέντες (Odyssey by Homer); perfect participle, ᾠνωμένος, ionic οἰνωμένος, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8468.definition:
1. Dep. to be gone, to have gone , Lat. abesse (not abire) , in perfect sense, and imperfect ὠιχόμην in pluperfect sense, directly opposite to ἥκω, to have come , while ἔρχομαι, to go  or come , serves as the present to both, (Homer), etc.;—;often with participle, οἴχεται φεύγων is fled and gone , (Iliad by Homer); ὤιχετ᾽ ἀποπτάμενος he hath taken flight and gone , (Iliad by Homer); οἴχεται θανών (see. infr. II. 1); also with an adjective, οἴχεται φροῦδος he's  clean gone, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with accusative pers. to have escaped from , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. Special usages, 
3. euphamistic for θνήσκω, to be gone hence , οἴχεται εἰς Ἀί̈δαο (Iliad by Homer); in attic, οἴχεται θανών (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;participle οἰχόμενος for θανών, departed, dead , [variant datesTragica Adespota; but in (Homer) simply absent  or away , Ὀδυσῆος πόθος οἰχομένοιο desire of the absent  Ulysses, (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. to be undone, ruined , (Sophocles Tragicus); especially in ὤιχωκα or οἴχωκα, Lat. perii, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
5. of things, to denote any quick, violent motion, to rush, sweep along , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8469.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to take omens from the flight and cries of birds , Lat. augurium, capere, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. generally, to divine from omens, augur , with accusative et infinitive, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8470.definition: divination by the flight  or cries of birds , Lat. augurium, (Euripides) (ML)

G8472.definition:
1. a large bird, bird of prey , such as a vulture  or eagle , and so distinguished from a common bird  ὄρνις); (Homer), etc. 
2. a bird of omen  or augury , (Homer), etc.:—;the flight to  (not from)  the right, i. e. towards the East, was fortunate, and vice versa. 
3. an omen, presage , drawn from these birds, Lat. auspicium or augurium , according as taken from seeing their flight  or hearing their cry , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; δέκομαι τὸν οἰωνόν I accept the omen , hail it as favourable, (Herdotus Historicus) 
commonly derivation from οἶος, —; most birds of prey being solitary, —;  compare κοινωνός from κοινός (ML)

G8473.definition:
to crouch down on one's hams, to squat , (Xenophon Historicus): ἐς γόνυ ὀκλάσας δέχεται τῇ σαρίσσῃ τὴν ἐπέλασιν, of a soldier waiting an attack, (Lucian); of a weary traveller, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with accusative, ὀκλ. τὰ ὀπίσθια, τοὺς προσθίους to bend  their hind or fore legs, (Xenophon Historicus) 
 (ML)

G8475.definition: eight thousand , (Herdotus Historicus); in singular, ἵππος ὀκτακισχιλίη "8000 horse, " (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8479.definition: eighteenth : ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ); on the eighteenth day , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8480.definition:
ὀλέθριος, -ον
 (also -α, -ον, as in Wis, l.with), [in LXX : 3Ki.20:42 (חֵרֶם), Wis.18:15 * ;]

G8481.definition: epic imperfect ὄλεκον, ionic ὀλέκεσκον, like ὄλλυμι, to ruin, destroy, kill , (Homer) (ML)

G8483.definition:
1. one out of a few , opposite to πολλοστός, (Plutarch) 
2. ὀλ. χρόνον for the smallest space  of Time, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8484.definition:
1. of Number, fewness , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. of Amount, smallness, scantiness :—;of Time, shortness , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8488.definition:
1. to slip, slip and fall , (Iliad by Homer); ἐξ ἀντύγων ὤλισθε he slipped  from the chariot, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically to make a slip , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to slip  or glide along , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8490.definition: a drawing, dragging, tugging: a drawing on  or towards  a thing, attraction, force of attraction , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8491.definition:
1. Act. = Lat. perdo, 
2. to destroy, make an end of , (Homer) 
3. to lose , θυμόν, ψυχήν, μένος, ἦτορ ὀλέσαι to lose  life, (Homer); πόνον ὀλέσαντες having lost  their labour, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. Mid., = Lat. pereo, 
5. to perish, come to an end , (Homer); also with accusative cognate, κακὸν οἶτον, κακὸν μόρον ὀλέσθαι to die by  an evil death, (Iliad by Homer):—; ὄλοιο, ὄλοισθε may'st thou, may ye, perish!  an imprecation, [variant datesTragica Adespota; so, ὀλοίμην, ὄλοιτο, ὄλοιντο, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. to be ruined, undone , (Homer), attic 
7. of things, to be lost , (Homer) 
8. perfect ὄλωλα, in sense of Mid., to have perished, to be undone, ruined , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; τῶν ὀλωλότων of the dead , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8496.definition: a loud crying , mostly a joyous cry , in honour of the gods, (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;rarely of lamentation , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8500.definition: mostly in plural ὄλυραι, a kind of grain, spelt  or rye , (Iliad by Homer); compare ζειά. (ML)

G8502.definition:
1. to make even  or level , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to level, equalise , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8505.definition:
1. a pledge for the maintenance of unity, a surety, a hostage , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2. of things, a pledge, security , τὴν γῆν ὅμηρον ἔχειν (Thucydides) 
 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8507.definition: born of the same mother , Lat. frater uterinus, (Herdotus Historicus); ὁμοματρία ἀδελφή (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8508.definition:
1. to be of one mind, agree together, live in harmony , (Thucydides); ὁμονοοῦσα ὀλιγαρχία a united  oligarchy, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. with dative to live in harmony with  others, with dative, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8509.definition:
oneness of mind  or thought, unity, concord , (Thucydides), etc. 
from ὁμόνους (ML)

G8511.definition:
ionic ὁμουρέω, future -ήσω to border upon, march with , [ οἱ Κελτοὶ, ὁμουρέουσι Κυνησίοισι (Herdotus Historicus) 
from ὅμορος (ML)

G8512.definition:
1. having the same borders with, marching with, bordering on , τοῖσι Δωριεῦσι, τῇ Λιβύῃ (Herdotus Historicus); absolute bordering , (Thucydides); πόλεμος ὅμορος a border  war, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. metaphorically bordering on, closely resembling , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. also as Substantive, a neighbour , (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὸ ὅμορον because of their neighbourhood , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8514.definition:
1. the navel , Lat. umbilicus, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. anything central (like a navel) : 
3. the knob  or boss in the middle  of the shield, Lat. umbo, (Iliad by Homer) 
4. a button  or knob  on the horse's yoke to fasten the reins to, (Iliad by Homer) 
5. in plural the knobs at each end of the stick round which books were rolled , Lat. umbilici, (Lucian) 
6. the centre  or middle point , as the island of Calypso is the ὀμφαλός of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); and Delphi (or rather a round stone in the Delphic temple) was called ὀμφαλός as marking the middle point of Earth , (Pindar), etc. (ML)

G8515.definition: an unripe grape , πάροιθε δέ τ᾽ ὄμφακές εἰσιν (Odyssey by Homer); ὅτ᾽ ὄμφακες αἰόλλονται (Hesiod); ὅταν δὲ τεύχῃ Ζεὺς ἀπp ὄμφακος οἶνον, i. e. autumn, when the unripe grapes become fit to make wine, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8518.definition: use, profit, advantage, good luck , (Odyssey by Homer):—;with genitive rei, enjoyment of  a thing, profit  or delight from  it, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; so, ὄν. εὑρεῖν ἀπό τινος (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8520.definition:
1. named, to be named , and οὐκ ὀνομαστός not to be named  or mentioned , i. e. abominable , Lat. infandus, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. of name  or note, notable, famous , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. (ML)

G8521.definition:
1. Lat. unguis, in (Homer) only in plural of the eagle's talons;—;  of human beings, a nail , (Hesiod), attic:—;of horses and oxen, a hoof , (Xenophon Historicus)—;Special phrases, εἰς ἄκρους τοὺς ὄνυχας ἀφίκετο (i.e. ὁ οἶνος); warmed me to my fingers' ends , (Euripides); ὄνυχας ἐπ᾽ ἄκρους στάς on tiptoe , Lat. summis digitis, (Euripides); ἐξ ἁπαλῶν ὀνύχων from childhood, (Horace) de tenero ungui , [variant datesAnthology Palantina; ὀδοῦσι καὶ ὄνυξι, i. e. in every possible way, (Lucian) 
2. a veined gem, onyx , (Lucian) (ML)

G8527.definition: quick to anger, choleric , (Euripides), etc.: —; sharp to punish , of the Areopagus, (Aeschulus Tragicus): τὸ ὀξύθυμον, by crasis τοὐξύθυμον, = ὀξυθυμία, (Euripides) (ML)

G8528.definition:
1. to sharpen : metaphorically to goad to anger, provoke , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to sharpen, quicken , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8529.definition:
1. sharpness, pointedness , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. of sound, sharpness , opposite to βαρύτης, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of the mind, sharpness, cleverness , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. of motion, quickness , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8531.definition: hinder, belonging to the hinder part , Lat. posticus, τὰ ὀπ. σκέλεα the hind-  legs, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8535.definition: a hoof, the solid hoof  of the horse and ass, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;after (Homer), like χηλή, the cloven hoof  of horned cattle, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

G8536.definition:
1. heavy-armed, armed , δρόμος ὁπλ. a race of men in armour , opposite to the naked  race, (Pindar); ὁπλ. στρατός an armed  host, (Euripides); ὁπλ. κόσμος warrior- dress, armour, (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive, a heavy-armed foot-soldier, man-at-arms , who carried a large shield  ὅπλον); whence the name, as the light-armed foot-soldier  πελταστής); had his from the light πέλτη, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; ὁπλῖται are opposite to ψιλοί, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8538.definition:
1. fighting in heavy arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. ὁπλ., one who teaches the use of arms, a drill-sergeant , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8539.definition:
1. bearing arms: a warrior, soldier , (Euripides) 
2. = δορυφόρος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8541.definition:
1. to roast, broil , (Homer), etc.; with genitive partitive, ὀπτῆσαί τε κρεῶν to roast  some meat, (Odyssey by Homer):—; ὀπτᾶν was used of cooking by means of fire  or dry heat , opposite to ἕψω to boil in water , which never appears in (Homer); and a [variant datesComica Adespota poet remarks that Homer's heroes ate only roast meat:—;Pass., aor1 infinitive ὀπτηθῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to bake  bread, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of bricks or pottery, to bake, burn , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. to bake, harden , of the sun, (Bion Bucolicus) 
4. metaphorically in Pass. to be burned  by love, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 
 (ML)

G8545.definition:
1. an organ, instrument, tool, for making  or doing  a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;of a person, ἁπάντων ἀεὶ κακῶν ὄργ. (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. an organ of sense , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. a musical instrument , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. a surgical instrument , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. a work, product , λαί̈νεα Ἀμφίονος ὄργανα the stony works  of Amphion, i. e. walls of Thebes, (Euripides) (ML)

G8546.definition:
1. to set straight : 
2. in height, to set upright, set up  one fallen or lying down, raise up , (Iliad by Homer); ὀρθοῦν κάρα, πρόσωπον (Euripides):—;of buildings, to raise up, rebuild , or, generally, to erect, build up , (Euripides):—;Pass. to be set upright , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: simply to rise from one's seat, stand up , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. in line, to make straight , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; Pass., ἢν τόδ᾽ ὀρθωθῆι βέλος if this dart go straight , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. metaphorically (from signf. I) to raise up, restore to health, safety, happiness , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;also to exalt, honour , (Pindar) 
5. (from signf. II) to guide aright , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὀρθ. ἀγῶνας to bring to a happy end , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὀ. βίον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to succeed, prosper , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ὀρθούμενον success , (Thucydides):—;of words and opinions, to be right, true , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν ἀγγέλωι κρυπτὸς ὀρθοῦται λόγος a secret message is rightly sent  by messenger, not by letter, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. in Pass. also, to be upright, deal justly , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8547.definition:
1. a marking out by boundaries, limitation , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the definition of a word , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8550.definition:
1. a cord, chain , especially a necklace, collar , (Homer), attic 
2. generally, anything strung like a necklace, a wreath, chaplet , (Pindar); στεφάνων ὅρμος a string  of crowns, i. e. of praises, (Pindar) 
3. a dance performed in a ring , (Lucian) 
4. a roadstead, anchorage, moorings , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
5. metaphorically a haven, place of shelter  or refuge , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 
6. = ἕρμα 1, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8553.definition:
a branch , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8556.definition: a bird which migrates with the quails , perhaps the land-rail , ludicrously applied to Latona, the Ortygian mother  (compare Ὀρτυγία)), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8558.definition:
1. orphanhood , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. bereavement, want of , στεφάνων (Pindar) 
 (ML)

G8559.definition: to make holy, purify, set free from guilt by offerings , Lat. expiate, (Euripides):—;Mid., στόμα ὁσιοῦσθαι to keep one's  tongue pure , not to speak profanely, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be purified , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8561.definition:
1. an earthen vessel , Lat. testa, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a tile  or potsherd , especially the tablet used in voting  (see. ὀστρακίζω); (Plato Philosophus) 
3. a sort of earthenware castanet , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. the hard shell of testaceous animals , as snails, muscles, tortoises, (Homeric Hymns) (ML)

G8562.definition: to catch scent of, smell, scent, track , with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; absolute, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8564.definition:
1. nowhere , answering to πο; where?  (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with genitive, οὐδαμοῦ γῆς (Herdotus Historicus); οὐδαμοῦ ἦν φρενῶν (Euripides) 
2. οὐδαμοῦ λέγειν τινά to esteem as naught , Lat. nullo in loco habere, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, θεοὺς νομίζων οὐδ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐδ. (or μηδαμοῦ); εἶναι, φαίνεσθαι, like Cicero's ne apparere quidem, not  to be taken into account , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of Manner, ἄλλοθι οὐδαμοῦ in no  other way , (Plato Philosophus) 
 (ML)

G8569.definition:
1. with a fair wind , Lat. vento secundo, οὔρ. πλοῦς, δρόμος a prosperous  voyage, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically prosperous, successful , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;neuter plural οὔρια as adverb, (Euripides) 
3. prospering, favouring, fair , of winds, (Euripides); comically of the bellows, οὐρίᾳ ῥιπίδι (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. οὐρία (i.e. πνοή); = οὖρος, a fair wind , οὐρίᾳ ἐφιέναι (i.e. ἑαυτόν); to run before the wind, (Plato Philosophus); so, ἐξ οὐρίων δραμοῦσα (i.e. δρόμων); after having run a fair course , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀφήσω ἐμαυτὸν οὔριον (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. Ζεὺς οὔριος, as sending fair winds , i. e. conducting things to a happy issue , [6th/5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8573.definition: older form of ὄχθος, a rising ground, a bank, dyke  by the side of a river, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural the raised banks of a river , (Homer); ὄχθαι καπέτοιο the banks  of the trench, (Iliad by Homer); also the dunes  or denes  along the sea (compare θίς); (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8575.definition:
1. like ἐχυρός, firm, lasting, stout , (Hesiod) 
2. of places, strong, secure , (Euripides): especially of a stronghold or position, strong, tenable , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. adverb -ρῶς, (Euripides) (ML)

G8576.definition: to make fast and sure, fortify , (Polybius Historicus): —;the Mid. just like Act., (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8577.definition: to do, go  or come late , (Xenophon Historicus):—; Pass., ὀψισθέντες belated, benighted , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8578.definition:
1. properly, cooked meat , or, generally, meat , opposite to bread and other provisions, (Homer) 
2. anything eaten with bread  or food , to give it flavour and relish, κρόμυον, ποτῷ ὄψον onions, a zest  or relish  to wine, (Iliad by Homer); ἐσθίουσι ἐπὶ τῷ σίτῳ ὄψον (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. seasoning, sauce , (Plato Philosophus); κολλύραν καὶ κόνδυλον ὄψον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῇ pudding and knuckle- sauce  withal, (Aristophanes Comicus); λιμῷ ὅσαπερ ὄψῳ διαχρῆσθε, i. e. "hunger is the best sauce," (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. generally, dainty fare , in plural dainties , (Plato Philosophus) 
5. at Athens, mostly, fish , the chief dainty of the Athenians, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. the fish-market , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8580.definition:
Πάγος, see: Ἄρειος.
 Ἄρειος Πάυος (T, Ἄριος Π.), -ου, ὁ 
 Hill of Pres or Mars, Areopagus; also, the Court of Areopagus, the highest tribunal of Athens: Act.17:19, 22.†
 (AS)

G8583.definition:
1. a plaything, toy , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), the Egyptians are called κακὰ παίγνια roguish playmates , 
3. a game, a sportive poem , [variant datesAnthology Palantina; of the merry chirp  of the cicada, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8584.definition: a cake of preserved fruit , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8586.definition: to wrestle , (Iliad by Homer): π. τινί to wrestle with  one, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., παλαισθείς beaten , (Euripides) (ML)

G8590.definition:
a concubine, mistress , Lat. pellex, opposite to a lawful wife  κουριδίη ἄλοχος); (Homer) 
Prob. from same Root as παλλάς = νεᾶνις. (ML)

G8591.definition:
1. to poise  or sway  a missile before it is thrown, (Euripides) 
2. to sway  other arms, not missiles, σάκος (Hesiod); πέλτας (Euripides):—;then, to toss  a child, (Iliad by Homer); Νὺξ ὄχημm ἔπαλλεν she drave  it furiously , (Euripides) 
3. κλήρους ἐν κυνέηι πάλλον they shook  the lots together in a helmet, till one leapt forth, (Homer): absolute to cast lots , (Iliad by Homer); ὅθ᾽ αὐτοὺς οἱ βραβεῖς κλήροις ἔπηλαν where the stewards ranged  them by casting  lots, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid. to draw lots , ἔλαχον ἅλα παλλομένων I obtained the sea when we cast lots , (Iliad by Homer); so in (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. Pass. to swing  or dash oneself , ἐν ἄντυγι πάλτο he dashed himself  upon the shield-rim, (Iliad by Homer): to quiver, leap , especially in fear, πάλλεται ἦτορ (Iliad by Homer); also of the person, παλλομένη κραδίην (Iliad by Homer); of dying fish, to quiver, leap , (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. intransitive, like the Pass., to leap, bound , (Euripides): to quiver , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8593.definition: with the whole people, in a mass  or body , (Herdotus Historicus); π. βοηθεῖν, στρατεύειν, of a whole people going out to war, a levee en masse , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8594.definition: to celebrate  or attend a festival , πανηγύρις π. to keep holy-days , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8596.definition: with all the house, household and all , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8598.definition:
1. of every kind, of all sorts, manifold , (Homeric Hymns), etc.:—;in plural, πολλοὶ καὶ π. (Herdotus Historicus):—;adverb -πῶς, in all kinds of ways , Poeta quoted in (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. παντοδαπὸς γίγνεται, = παντοῖος γίγνεται, assumes every shape , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8599.definition:
1. the papyrus , an Egyptian rush with triangular stalks: paper was made by peeling off its outer coat  βύβλος); and gluing the slips together. 
2. anything made of it, linen, cord , etc., [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8602.definition:
1. to look aside, take a side look , (Aristophanes Comicus); π. θατέρῳ (i.e. ὀφθαλμῷ); to look suspiciously  with one eye, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to see wrong , (Lucian) (ML)

G8603.definition:
1. a message transmitted  by beacons, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. an order, command , ἀπὸ παραγγέλματος by word of command , (Thucydides) 
3. an instruction, precept , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8606.definition:
1. a pattern  or model  of the thing to be executed, Lat. exemplar, an architect's plan , (Herdotus Historicus); a sculptor's or painter's model , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. a precedent, example , (Thucydides); ἐπὶ παραδείγματος by way of example , (Aeschines Orator) 
3. an example , i. e. a lesson  or warning , π. ἔχειν τινός to take a lesson  from another, (Thucydides); τὸ σὸν π. ἔχων (Sophocles Tragicus); ζῶντά τινα τοῖς λοιποῖς π. ποιεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. an argument, proof from example , (Thucydides) 
5. the model  or copy  of an existing thing, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8607.gloss: to hold forth as an example
G8607.definition:
1. to exhibit side by side : generally, to exhibit, bring forward , in Mid., (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to represent  as so and so, π. τινὰ οὐκ ὄντα (Polybius Historicus): also in bad sense, like παραδειγματίζω, (Plutarch) 
3. to exhibit and hand over , τί τινι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8608.definition: to do an incredible thing; render notorious

G8609.definition: a running beside  or over, traversing , (Plutarch); ἐν παραδρομῇ cursorily , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8611.definition: to heat to excess :—;Pass., aor1 participle παραθερμανθείς, of a man become quarrelsome  in his cups, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8612.definition: juxta-position, neighbourhood , (Polybius Historicus); ἐκ παραθέσεως on comparison , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8614.definition:
1. to take away from beside, withdraw, remove , (Euripides):—; with genitive partitive to take away part of  a thing, (Euripides):—;Pass., παρῃρημένοι τὰ ὅπλα having  their arms taken from them, (Thucydides) 
2. π. ἀρὰν εἰς παῖδα to draw aside  the curse on thy son's head, (Euripides) 
3. Mid. to draw over to one's own side, seduce, detach , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. to take away , (Xenophon Historicus): Mid., παραιρεῖσθαι τὴν θρασύτητα to lessen, damp  it, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. generally, to take away from, steal away from , τί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8615.definition: Dep. to be seated beside  or near  another, with dative, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G8617.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to order  one to  do a thing, advise, prescribe , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; π. ταῦτα to give  this advice , (Plato Philosophus);—;also, π. τινι, with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. to exhort , τοιαῦτα παρακελευσάμενος having delivered  this address , (Thucydides):—;absolute to encourage one another by shouting , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. παρακεκέλευστο in passive sense, orders had been given , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8621.definition:
1. to strike aside: to disappoint, mislead , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be led astray, go wrong , (Plato Philosophus):—;so also in Mid., (Isocrates Orator) 
2. in Mid. also, to strike away from oneself, parry , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8624.definition:
1. to make things alternate, to transpose , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to change  or alter a little , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of Place, to pass by, go past, elude , (Xenophon Historicus):—; to get rid of , (Plutarch) 
4. to go beyond, exceed  in point of time, (Plutarch) 
5. intransitive to pass by one another, to overlap , (Herdotus Historicus) 
6. to differ, vary , (Herdotus Historicus):—;impersonal, οὐ σμικρὸν παραλλάττει it makes  no small difference , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. π. τοῦ σκοποῦ to go aside from  the mark, (Plato Philosophus) 
8. to deviate from the course, to be liable to deviation , (Plato Philosophus); λόγοι παραλλάσσοντες delirious , (Euripides) 
9. to slip aside  or away , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8625.definition: a loosening by the side: paralysis, palsy , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8626.definition: to spend amiss, to waste, squander , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass., of persons, to be sacrificed uselessly , 3rd plural aor1 παραναλώθησαν (Plutarch) (ML)

G8627.definition:
1. acting contrary to law, lawless , (Euripides) 
2. of things, contrary to law, unlawful , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—;adverb, παρανόμως, illegally , (Thucydides) 
3. in attic law, παράνομα γράφειν, εἰπεῖν to propose an illegal measure , (Demosthenes Orator); παρανόμων γράφεσθαί τινα to indict one for proposing such a measure , (Demosthenes Orator): the indictment itself was παρανόμων γραφή (Aeschines Orator):—;in superlative, παρανομώτατα γεγραφότα (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8629.definition: a knife worn beside the sword, a dirk , (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G8630.definition:
1. altogether, absolutely , generally with Art., τὸ π. (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;with a negative, τὸ π. οὐδέν not at all , (Herdotus Historicus); οὔκ εἰμι τὸ π. ἄθεος (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in reckoning, ἐπὶ διηκόσια τὸ παράπαν up to two hundred altogether , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8631.definition: that which is spread before  a thing, a hanging curtain , (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically a screen, cover , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8634.definition: a falling beside;  κατὰ τὴν π. τινος in the course  of an action, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8635.definition: to throw beside : metaphorically to run the risk  of doing a thing, with participle, π. λαμβάνων (Sophocles Tragicus): to throw aside, reject , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8637.definition: to pass over in silence , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8638.definition:
1. a putting aside  or away, banishing, relegatio , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. a setting out  things for sale, retail-trade , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3.  παρίσταμαι); intransitive a being beside : 
4. a position  or post near  a king, (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. presence of mind, courage , (Polybius Historicus): also, desperation , (Polybius Historicus) 
6. as law-term, a small money deposit  on entering law-suits, (Isaeus Orator) (ML)

G8641.definition:
1. to place side by side, draw up in battle-order , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Mid. to draw up one's men in battle-order , (Xenophon Historicus); so of ships, (Thucydides):—;Mid. and Pass. to be drawn up along , παρατετάχατο παρὰ τὴν ἀκτήν (Herdotus Historicus); ἑκατέρωθεν παρατεταγμένοι (Thucydides); so, παρετάξαντο ἀλλήλοις (Xenophon Historicus): absolute, παρατεταγμένοι or παραταξάμενοι in order of battle , (Thucydides) 
2. in Mid. and Pass., also, to stand prepared , παρατετάχθαι πρὸς τὸ ἀποκρίνεσθαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8642.definition:
1. to run by  or past , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to outrun, overtake , (Iliad by Homer): π. τὰ τότε κακά to go beyond, exceed  them, (Euripides) 
3. to run through  or over, run across  (a space of ground expressed or implied), (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. to run over , i. e. treat in a cursory way , (Isocrates Orator):—; to slight, neglect , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
5. to escape unnoticed , τινά (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8645.definition:
1. to sit constantly beside, attend constantly, be always near , Lat. assidere, with dative, (Euripides) 
2. of judges, to be an assessor , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8647.definition: to stretch out in line , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8649.definition:
1. as preposition, 
2. with genitive loci, outside, before , παρὲκ λιμένος (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ὁδοῦ out of  the road, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. like χωρίς, besides, except, exclusive of , παρὲξ τοῦ ἀργύρου (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. with accusative out by the side of, along side of , παρὲξ ἅλα (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ τὴν νῆσον away from  the island, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ δοῦρα out of the way of  spears, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲκ νόον out of  sense and reason, foolishly, (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ Ἀχιλῆα without the knowledge of  Achilles, (Iliad by Homer) 
5. as adverb, 
6. of Place, out beside , στῆ δὲ παρέξ hard by , (Iliad by Homer); νῆχε παρέξ was swimming out along shore , (Odyssey by Homer) 
7. metaphorically beside the mark , παρὲξ ἀγορεύειν (Iliad by Homer) 
8. ἄλλα παρὲξ μεμνώμεθα let us talk of something else , (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ἢ ὅσον except  so long as, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8651.definition: marks of virginity; tokens of virginity

G8653.definition:
παρ-ιστάνω, see: παρίστημι.
 παρ-ίστημι 
 [in LXX for עָמַד, etc. ;] 
__I. Transitive verb. in present tense., imperfect., future tense., 1 aorist.; 
 __1. to place beside, present, provide: with accusative, Act.9:41 23:24, 2Co.4:14, Col.1:28; with accusative and dative, Mat.26:53, Luk.2:22, Act.1:3 23:33, 1Co.8:8; before accusative pred., Rom.6:13, 16 (late pres., παριστάνετε), Rom.6:19 12:1, 2Co.11:2, Eph.5:27, Col.1:22, 2Ti.2:15. 
 __2. to present to the mind (cl.) : by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), with accusative, Act.24:13. 
 __II. Intransitive. in  perfect., pluperfect., 2 aorist.; 
 __1. to stand by or beside one : with dative of person(s), Act.1:10 9:39 23:2 27:23; ptcp., Mrk.14:47, 69-70 15:35, 39 Jhn.18:22 19:26. 
 __2. to appear: with nom. pred., before ἐνώπιον, Act.4:10; with dative of person(s), Act.27:24; so fut. mid. (of. LS, see word, B, ii, 2), Rom.14:10. 
 __3. to be at hand, be present, have come: Act.4:26 (LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, Luk.1:19; absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες, Luk.19:24; before αὐτῷ, Act.23:2, 4; of time, Mrk.4:29 
 __4. to stand by for help or defence (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Rom.16:2, 2Ti.4:17.†
 (AS)

G8654.definition:
1. to pass by , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. with accusative to go past , (Lucian) (ML)

G8657.definition:
1. to behave ill at wine, play drunken tricks , (Isaeus Orator) 
2. to act like a drunken man , (Plutarch); παροινήσας in a drunken fit , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. transitive to treat with drunken violence :—; Pass. to be so treated , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8659.definition:
1. to look at by the way, notice, remark , (Xenophon Historicus); τί τινι something in one, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to overlook, disregard, neglect , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
3. to see amiss, see wrong , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. to look sideways , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8662.definition:
1. a peg  on which to hang clothes, arms, etc., (Homer), etc.; ἀπὸ πασσαλόφι ζυγὸν ᾕρεον (Iliad by Homer); ἀπὸ πασσάλου αἴνυτο τόξον (Odyssey by Homer); ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a gag , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8663.definition:
1. to sprinkle , φάρμακα πάσσων laying  salves upon  a wound, (Iliad by Homer): —;with genitive partitive, πάσσε ἁλός sprinkle some  salt, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to besprinkle , χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. metaphorically to embroider, broider , (Iliad by Homer); π. ἀέθλους to work  battles in embroidery , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8670.definition:
1. of  or belonging to one's father , Lat. patrius, (Pindar), etc. 
2. = πατρικός, derived from one's fathers, hereditary , οἱπ. θεοί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: —; τὰ πάτρια, Lat. instituta majorum, κατὰ τὰ πάτρια (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; rarely in singular, τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting the rule of our fathers , (Thucydides) Cf. πατρῷος. (ML)

G8672.definition: hoar-frost, rime , Lat. pruina, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, κουροβόρος π. the clotted blood  of the eaten children, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8673.definition:
1. thickness , (Odyssey by Homer):—; absolute, πάχος in thickness , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. π. σαρκός stoutness , (Euripides) (ML)

G8674.definition:
1. thick, stout , (Homer):—; later, stout, fat , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things, thick, massive , (Homer):—;adverb -έως, roughly , of stating or arguing, (Aristotle Philosopher); παχύτερον or -έρως, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of liquids, thick, curdled, clotted , (Iliad by Homer) 
4. οἱ παχέες the men of substance, the wealthy class , (Herdotus Historicus); τοὺς παχεῖς καὶ πλουσίους (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. in [variant datesComica Adespota and Prose, thick-witted, gross, dull, stupid , like Lat. pinguis, crassus, [variant datesComica Adespota 
6. comparative παχύτερος, sup. -ύτατος:—;irregular comparative πάσσων, ον, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Sup. πάχιστος, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8675.definition:
1. to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to shackle, trammel, constrain , (Homer); with infinitive to constrain  one to do a thing, (Homer) (ML)

G8676.definition:
a plain  or flat , and collectively a plain flat open country , (Homer), etc. 
 (ML)

G8677.definition:
1. on foot , πεζοί fighters on foot , opposite to horsemen, (Homer):—;also on land, going by land , opposite to sea-faring, (Homer):—;so, ὁ πεζὸς στρατός, or ὁ πεζός alone, sometimes foot-soldiery, infantry , opposite to cavalry  ἡ ἵππος); (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. ὁ πεζός, also, a land-force  or army , opposite to a naval force, (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὸ πεζόν (Herdotus Historicus); στρατιὰ καὶ ναυτικὴ καὶ πεζή (Thucydides); τὰ πεζὰ κράτιστοι strongest by land , (Thucydides) 
3. of animals, land , as opposite to birds and fishes, τὰ π. καὶ τὰ πτηνά beasts  and birds, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. metaphorically of language, not rising above the ground, prosaic , (Lucian) 
5. dative feminine πεζῇ (entry ὁδῷ); as adverb, on foot , (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. by land , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8680.definition: a pirate , Lat. pirata, i. e. one who attacks  ships, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8681.definition:
1. near, hard by, close , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. absolute, χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [variant datesTragica Adespota 
4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες); one's neighbours , (Thucydides), etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8683.definition: to hew  or shape with an axe , Lat. dolare, (Odyssey by Homer) (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8685.definition:
1. an axe  for felling trees, with two edges, opposite to the ἡμιπέλεκκον, (Homer) 
2. a sacrificial axe , (Homer)—;That it was not, properly, a battle axe  appears from the phrase, οὐ δόρασι μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πελέκεσι to fight not with spears only, but with common axes , i. e. to the last, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. in (Theophrastus Philosophus) Char., πέλεκυς as a child's nickname seems to mean a sharp blade.  (ML)

G8688.definition: one who bears a light shield  πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer , Lat. cetratus, (Euripides), etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί. (ML)

G8689.definition:
1. a small light shield  of leather without a rim  ἴτυς); a target , Lat. cetra, originally used by the Thracians, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. a body of  πελτασταί, (Euripides) 
3. a horse's ornament , (Euripides) 
4. = παλτόν, a shaft, pole , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8690.definition: a kind of axe , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8691.definition: any kind of dressed food;  but mostly in plural, pastry, cakes, sweetmeats , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8692.definition: of  or for mourning, mournful :—;adverb, πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in mourning  for a person, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8694.definition:
1. Dep., used in present and imperfect : 
2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread ; generally, to toil, work, labour , (Homer) 
3. to be poor  or needy , Solon , (Euripides), etc. 
4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8695.definition:
1. five years old , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of Time, lasting five years , (Thucydides):—; neuter adverb πεντάετες, for five years , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8696.definition: five cubits long  or broad , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8705.definition: the commander of fifty men , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8708.definition:
1. fiftieth , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. as Substantive, ἡ πεντηκοστή, 
3. (i.e. μερίς); at Athens the duty of one-fiftieth , or two per century , on all exports and imports, (Isaeus Orator); εὕρηκε καινὴν ἱππικῆς τινὰ πεντηκοστήν he invented a new two per century duty , in lieu of his cavalry service, i. e. paid this instead of it, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. (i.e. ἡμέρα); the fiftieth day  (after the Passover), Pentecost , (New Testament) (ML)

G8709.definition:
1. ripe , Lat. maturus, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. metaphorically softened , ὀργή (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8711.definition:
1. of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow , Lat. mitis, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically in vocative, mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle , ὦ πέπον my good friend , (Iliad by Homer); κριὲ πέπον my pet  ram, (Odyssey by Homer);—; in bad sense, soft, weak , (Iliad by Homer); ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings , (Iliad by Homer): —; μόχθος πέπων softened  pain, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.: with dative, ἐχθροῖς π. gentle  to one's foes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8712.definition:
1. to bring to an end, finish, accomplish, execute , [variant datesTragica Adespota, etc.:—;Pass. to be brought to an end, be finished , πάντα πεπείρανται (Odyssey by Homer): to be fulfilled, accomplished , (Euripides) etc. 
2. in speaking, to end  a discourse, finish  speaking, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
3. to repeat from beginning to end , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; to relate , (Euripides) 
4. absolute to effect one's purpose , especially with a negative, οὐδὲν π. to come to  no issue, do  no good, make  no progress , (Euripides) 
5. intransitive to make way, reach  or penetrate , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. intransitive to come to an end, end , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8717.definition: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)

G8719.definition:
1. anything which is thrown round, a covering , (Plato Philosophus); χειρῶν περιβολαί embraces , (Euripides); so περιβολαί alone, (Xenophon Historicus); περιβολαὶ χθονός, i. e. the grave, (Euripides); π. [ ξίφεος] a scabbard, (Euripides): absolute of walls round  a town, ἑπτάπυργοι π. (Euripides) 
2. a space enclosed, compass , οἰκίης μεγάλης περιβολή a house of large compass , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. a circumference, circuit , (Thucydides); π. ποιεῖσθαι to make a circuit , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. metaphorically, 
5. a compassing, endeavouring after , τῆς ἀρχῆς, Lat. affectatio imperii, (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. ἡ π. τοῦ λόγου the whole compass  of the matter, long and short  of it, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8720.definition:
1. going round, compassing, encircling , (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive, περίβολος = περιβολή, ἐχίδνης περίβολοι the spires  or coils  of a serpent, (Euripides); in plural walls round a town , (Herdotus Historicus); so in singular, (Thucydides) 
3. an enclosure, circuit, compass , π. νεωρίων (Euripides); of a temple, the precincts , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8723.definition:
1. with two right hands , i.e. using both hands alike , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. very dexterous , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8724.definition: Dep. to grasp  a thing with the hand , with genitive rei, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8725.definition:
1. to be around  a place, with dative, (Thucydides); τὰ περιόντα circumstances , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to be better than, superior to  another, surpass, excel , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε (Odyssey by Homer); οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δd ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι λπαρr εθυαλσs μάχην)) (Iliad by Homer); with dative rei, σοφίᾳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be superior , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐκ περιόντος at an advantage , (Thucydides) 
3. to overlive, outlive , τινι (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to survive, remain alive , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;of things, to be extant, to be in existence , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. to be over and above, to remain in hand , of property, money, etc., (Thucydides); οἰόμενοι περιεῖναι χρήματά τῳ imagining that any one has a balance  in his hands, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. to be a result  or consequence , περίεστιν ὑμῖν ἐκ τούτων what you have got by all this is . ., (Demosthenes Orator); τοσοῦτον ὑμῖν περίεστιν τοῦ πρὸς ἐμὲ μίσους you have  so much hatred against me left , Philipp. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); with infinitive, περίεστι ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ἐρίζειν it remains  for you to quarrel with them, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8726.definition: a girdle round the loins, apron , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8730.definition: to be seated  or to sit all round , (Herdotus Historicus): of an army, to beleaguer, invest  a town, (Herdotus Historicus); of ships, to blockade , (Herdotus Historicus): with accusative pers. to sit down by  one, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8732.definition: to shear  or clip all round , (Herdotus Historicus); Mid., περικείρεσθαι τρίχας to have one's  hair clipt , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8736.definition:
1. to seize around, embrace , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to encompass  or surround  an enemy, so as to intercept  him, (Herdotus Historicus); μετεώρους τὰς ναῦς π. to intercept  them at sea, (Thucydides); ἐπεὰν δὲ αὐτὸν περιλάβῃς when you get hold of  him, catch  him, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be caught , οἴμοι, περιείλημμαι μόνος (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to comprehend, include , of a number of particulars, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8740.definition: to go all round , with accusative, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8741.definition:
1. a going round, a flank march , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass , τοῦ τείχεος, τῆς λίμνης (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, τὴν π. in circumference , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. γῆς π. a chart  or map  of the earth (compare πίναξ); (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. a going round in a circle, circuit , (Plutarch) 
5. of Time, a cycle  or period of time , (Pindar), etc. 
6. a prescribed course of life, system , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. a fit  of intermittent fever, (Demosthenes Orator) 
8. = περιφορά, a course at dinner , (Xenophon Historicus); π. λόγων table-talk , (Xenophon Historicus) 
9. the orbit of a heavenly body , (Xenophon Historicus) 
10. a well-rounded sentence, period , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8742.definition:
1. to build round , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to enclose by building round , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be built up, walled in , (Thucydides); τὸ περιοικοδομημένον the space built round, the enclosure , Lat. ovile, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8745.definition:
1. a walking about, walking , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. a place for walking, a covered walk , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. discourse during a walk, a philosophical discussion , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. οἱ ἐκ τοῦ περιπάτου the Peripatetics, school of Aristotle , because he taught walking in a  περίπατος of the Lyceum  at Athens, (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

G8746.definition:
1. to twine  or enfold round :—;Pass. to fold oneself round , with dative, ἱστῷ περιπλεχθείς (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, δίκτυον εὖ μάλα περιπλεκόμενον close folding , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to complicate, entangle , (Lucian) 
3. to wrap up in words , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8747.definition: a station for  περίπολοι, a guard-house , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8748.definition: edged with purple , π. ἐσθής a robe with a purple border , the Roman toga praetextata  or laticlavia , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8751.definition: to besprinkle all round , especially in sacred rites:—;Mid. to purify oneself , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8753.definition: dry and hard all round, exceeding hard , of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically obstinate, stubborn , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8757.definition:
1. a standing round, a crowd standing round , Lat. corona, (Theophrastus Philosophus), etc. 
2. circumstances, a state of affairs , (Polybius Historicus):—;in bad sense, κατὰ τὰς π. in critical times , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. outward pomp and circumstance , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8758.definition:
1. to dress, clothe, wrap up , (Pindar); ἔπηξα δ᾽ αὐτὸν εὖ περιστείλας I planted the sword having wrapt  it well with earth , i. e. planted it firmly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to dress  or lay out  a corpse, Lat. componere, (Odyssey by Homer), attic: simply, to bury , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. metaphorically to wrap up, cloak, cover , τἄδικ᾽ εὖ π. (Euripides):—;Mid., τὰ σὰ περιστέλλου κακά (Euripides) 
4. to take care of, protect, defend , (Herdotus Historicus); π. τοὺς νόμους to maintain  the laws, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ πάτρια (Demosthenes Orator); π. ἀοιδάν to uphold  minstrelsy, (Pindar) (ML)

G8762.definition:
1. to whirl round , of one preparing to throw, (Homer); π. ἵππον to wheel  it round , (Plutarch):—; Pass. to be turned round, spin round , (Iliad by Homer); π. εἰς τἀληθῆ to come round to  it, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. π. τὼ χεῖρε to tie  his hands behind  him, (Lysias Orator). (ML)

G8763.definition:
1. with pillars round the wall, surrounded with a colonnade , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. as Substantive, περίστυλον, ου, τό, or περίστυλος, ὁ, a peristyle, colonnade round a temple  or court-yard , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8764.definition:
1. to drag about , ἄνω καὶ κάτω (Lucian) 
2. to tear away from , τί τινος (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8765.definition:
1. to slit and tear off , (Plutarch) 
2. Pass., of a river, περισχίζεσθαι τὸν χῶρον to split round  a piece of land, i. e. split into two branches so as to surround  it, (Herdotus Historicus);—;so, of a stream of men, to part and go different ways , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8766.definition:
1. to wall all round , πλίνθοις Βαβυλῶνα (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to surround with a wall , so as to beleaguer, (Thucydides) 
3. to build round , ὁ περιτετειχισμένος κύκλος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8768.definition:
1. the line round a circular body, a periphery, circumference , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the outer surface , (Plutarch) 
3. a round body , (Plutarch) 
from περιφερής (ML)

G8769.definition:
1. moving round, surrounding , with genitive, (Euripides) 
2. surrounded by , with dative, (Euripides) 
3. round, circular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of bodies, spherical, globular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of style, rounded , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8770.definition:
1. meats carried round , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a going round, rotatory motion, circuit, revolution , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
3. the revolving vault  of heaven, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. metaphorically, ἐν ταῖς περιφοραῖς in society , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8773.definition: to surround with a stockade , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8774.definition: exceeding joyous  or glad , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τινι at a thing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τὸ π. excessive joy , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8775.definition: to pour round  or over , τί τινι, properly of liquids, (Homer); of metal-workers, χρυσὸν κέρασιν περιχεύας having spread  gold leaf round  its horns, (Iliad by Homer); so in Mid., ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε τις χρυσὸν περιχεύεται ἀργύρῳ (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass. to be poured around , περὶ δ᾽ ἀμβρόσιος κέχυθ᾽ ὕπνος (Iliad by Homer); τῶν ὀστέων περικεχυμένων heaped all round , (Herdotus Historicus); of persons, περιχυθέντες crowding round , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8778.definition:
1. to soften, ripen  or change , by means of heat: 
2. of the sun, to ripen  fruit, (Odyssey by Homer); compare πεπαίνω. 
3. by the action of fire, to cook, dress, bake , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., πέσσεσθαι πέμματα to cook oneself  cakes, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of the stomach, to digest , like Lat. concoquere, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. metaphorically, χόλον πέσσειν to cherish  or nurse  one's wrath, Lat. fovere, (Iliad by Homer); βέλος πέσσειν to have  a dart in one to nurse , (Iliad by Homer); but in good sense, γέρα πεσσέμεν to enjoy  them, (Iliad by Homer); also, ἀκίνδυνον αἰῶνα πέσσειν to lead a sodden  life of ease, (Pindar) (ML)

G8779.definition:
1. a leaf , mostly in plural, (Homer):—; poetry, νεικέων πέταλα contentious votes (compare πεταλισμός); (Pindar) 
2. a leaf of metal , (Lucian) (ML)

G8780.definition: to spread out  sails or clothes, (Odyssey by Homer); χεῖρε πετάσσας, of one swimming, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, θυμὸν πετάσαι to open  one's heart, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., mostly in perfect, to be spread on all sides , (Homer): participle spread wide, opened wide , of folding doors, πύλαι πεπταμέναι (Iliad by Homer); πετάσθησαν (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8781.definition:
a perch  for fowls to roost at night, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8783.definition:
1. throwing stones , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. as Substantive, πετροβόλος, an engine for throwing stones , Lat. ballista, (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8784.definition:
1. the pine , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. any thing made from its wood, a torch of pine-wood , [variant datesTragica Adespota 
3. a writing-tablet , (Euripides) (ML)

G8785.definition: of  or from pine  or pine-wood , (Sophocles Tragicus); π. δάκρυα tears of the pine , i. e. the resinous drops that ooze from it, (Euripides) (ML)

G8787.definition:
1. anything joined together, framework , of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Lat. pegma, a moveable scaffold used in theatres, (Juvenal) 
2. metaphorically, π. γενναίως παγέν a bond  in honour bound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. π. τῆς χιόνος frozen  snow, (Polybius Historicus) 
 (ML)

G8788.definition:
1. to leap, spring, bound , ὑψόσε ποσσὶν ἐπήδα (Iliad by Homer); π. ἐς σκάφος (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative cognate, πήδημα πηδᾶν to take  a leap, (Euripides); with accusative loci, πεδία πηδᾶν to bound over  them, (Sophocles Tragicus); π. πλάκα (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer); of the heart, to leap, throb , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; of sudden changes, τί πηδᾶις εἰς ἄλλους τρόπου; (Euripides) (ML)

G8789.definition: of clay , Lat. fictilis, οἱ πήλινοι clay figures , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8790.definition:
1. to make fat, fatten , (Euripides); π. χθόνα to fatten  the soil, of a dead man, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to be  or become fat , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. metaphorically, 
3. to increase, enlarge , πλοῦτον (Pindar) 
4. to make wanton, excite , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to wax fat and wanton , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἔχθεσιν πιαίνεσθαι to batten on  quarrels, (Pindar) (ML)

G8791.definition:
an ape, monkey , (Aristophanes Comicus); as feminine, πίθηκος μήτηρ (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;of persons, an ape, jackanapes , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8792.definition:
πιθός, see: πειθός.
 πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν 
 (πείθω), = cl. πιθανός, 
persuasive: 1Co.2:4 (not found elsewhere).†
 (AS)

G8796.definition: pitch , Lat. pix, (Iliad by Homer), etc.: proverbial, ἄρτι μῦς πίττης γεύεται, i. e. he has got the first taste of misery, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8797.definition: the pine, stone pine , (Homer):—;proverbial, πίτυος τρόπον ἐκτρίβεσθαι to be destroyed like a pine , i. e. utterly , because the pine when cut down never grows again, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8798.definition:
1. neuter πῖον, genitive πίονος, fat, plump , Lat. pinguis, (Homer); π. δημός rich  fat, (Iliad by Homer); of oil, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of soil, fat, rich.  (Iliad by Homer); also, πίονα ἔργα pingues segetes , (Iliad by Homer); ὀπώρας πίων ποτός, of wine, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. of persons and places, rich, wealthy , (Homer); πίονι μέτρῳ in plenteous  measure, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
4. The comparative and Sup. are πι-ότερος, πι-ότατος, as if from πῖος. (ML)

G8799.definition: to turn sideways  or aside , πλ. πρὸς τοὺς ἀντίους ἀνέμους (i.e. τὴν ναῦν); to beat up  against adverse winds, (Lucian): metaphorically, πλ. ἢ φωνὴν ἢ πρᾶξιν to adapt  them to circumstances , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8800.definition:
1. placed sideways, slanting, aslant , Lat. obliquus, (Thucydides) 
2. πλάγια, ων, τά, the sides , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in military sense, τοῖς πλαγίοις ἐπιέναι to attack the flanks , (Thucydides); εἰς τὰ πλ. παράγειν or παραπέμπειν to make an army file off right and left , (Xenophon Historicus); πλαγίους λαβεῖν τοὺς πολεμίους to take the enemy in flank , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with Preps. in adverbial sense, εἰς πλάγιον obliquely , (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς τὰ πλάγια, opposite to εἰς τὸ ἀντίον, (Thucydides); ἐκ πλαγίου in flank , (Thucydides); κατὰ πλάγια (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. metaphorically not straightforward, crooked, treacherous , φρένες (Pindar); πλάγια φρονεῖν (Euripides) (ML)

G8801.definition: a making to wander, a dispersing , τῶν νεῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8802.definition:
the oriental plane , Lat. platanus, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
From πλατύς, because of its broad leaves.  (ML)

G8804.definition: mostly, most often, very often , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8805.definition: more frequently, oftener , (Plato Philosophus): several times, frequently , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8809.definition:
1. an advantage, gain, privilege , (Plato Philosophus): in plural gains, successes , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. an act of overreaching, selfish trick , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8810.definition:
1. a rib : mostly in plural the ribs, the side , (Iliad by Homer), etc.;—;also in singular, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of places, πλευρὸν νεῶν the side  of the bay where the ships lay, (Sophocles Tragicus); τὸ δεξιὸν πλ. the right flank  (of an army), (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8811.definition:
a mistake in music, false note : metaphorically a fault, offence, error , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πλημμελέω (ML)

G8812.definition: to make a false note in music : metaphorically to go wrong, offend, err , τι in a thing, (Euripides), etc.; εἴς τινα (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., πλημμελεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος to be ill-treated  by one, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8815.definition:
1. a filling up, filling , (Plato Philosophus): often of eating and drinking, satiety , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. the completion of a number , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8816.definition:
1. near, close to , with genitive or dative, πλησίοι ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοισι (Homer):—;absolute near, neighbouring , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;as Substantive a neighbour , ἰδὼν ἐς πλ. ἄλλον (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. adverb πλησίον, doric πλα_τίον, = πέλας, near, nigh, hard by , with genitive, (Homer), etc.; with dative, (Euripides) 
3. with the Art., ὁ πλησίον (i.e. ὤν); one's neighbour , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; so in doric, ὁ πλα_τίον (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;also, with Substantives, ὁ πλ. παράδεισος (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. comparative πλησιαίτερος, Sup. -αίτατος, (Xenophon Historicus)—;comparative adverb πλησιαιτέρω, (Herdotus Historicus); -αίτερον, (Xenophon Historicus); Sup. -αίτατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8818.definition:
1. to make into bricks , τὴν γῆν (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to make bricks , (Aristophanes Comicus);—;so in Mid., thuc. 
2. to build of brick , τείχη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to make in the form of a plinth  or brick , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 (ML)

G8819.definition:
1. a small brick , (Thucydides) 
2. = πλαίσιον, a rectangle  or square , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8820.definition: a brick , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πλίνθους ἑλκύσαι, εἰρύσαι, Lat. ducere lateres, to make bricks , (Herdotus Historicus); ὀπτᾶν to bake  them, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8822.definition:
1. a twining: anything woven, a web , (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically the complication of  a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8824.definition:
1. floating , (Odyssey by Homer); πλωτοί swimmers , i. e. fish, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. navigable , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of seasons, fit for navigation , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8827.definition: the organ of  breathing, the lungs , Lat. pulmo, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural, [variant datesTragica Adespota; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πλευμόνων (Euripides) (ML)

G8828.definition:
1. grass, herb , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or lucerne , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. the grass , i. e. a grassy place , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four grasses , i. e. summers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8829.definition:
1. to long for, yearn after  what is absent, to miss  or regret  what is lost, Lat. desiderare, (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things, to require , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with infinitive to be anxious  to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness needs  to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. absolute, τὸ ποθοῦν one's desiring, one's longing , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the longing  soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8830.definition:
1. a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery , (Plato Philosophus): in plural pieces of broidery , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. varied aspect, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. versatility, subtlety, craft , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8831.definition:
1. to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε he wrought a  χορός of cunning workmanship , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to embroider  a robe, (Pindar), etc. 
3. generally, to diversify, vary , (Euripides):—;of style, to embellish , (Pindar):—; to speak as in riddles , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8832.definition:
1. a broidered stuff, brocade , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. broidered work, broidery , (Homer) 
3. generally, a variety, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8837.definition: of  or for a shepherd , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8838.definition:
1. wool  in its raw state, a fleece , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: a lock  or tuft of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. proverbial in heterocl. accusative of 3rd declension, εἰς ὄνου πόκας to an ass shearing , i. e. to no-place, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8839.definition:
1. of  or for war , (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη most fit for service , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); the art of war, war , (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά warlike exercises , (Thucydides) 
3. τὸ πολεμικόν the signal for battle , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. the military class , opposite to the civilian, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. of persons, skilled in war, warlike , (Thucydides), etc. 
6. like an enemy, stirring up hostility , (Xenophon Historicus):—;adverb, πολεμικῶς ἔχειν to be hostile , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8840.definition:
1. of  or belonging to war , (Pindar), etc.: —; τὰ πολέμια whatever belongs to war, war and its business , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. of  or like an enemy, hostile , (Pindar), etc.:—;as Substantive an enemy , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π. the enemy , (Thucydides): —; τὸ π. hostility , (Thucydides) 
3. generally, opposed, adverse , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of  or from the enemy , (Aeschulus Tragicus); πολέμια, ων, τά, enemy's wares, contraband , (Aristophanes Comicus): —; ἡ πολεμία (i.e. γῆ, χώρα); the enemy's country , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. adverb -ίως, in hostile manner , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8841.definition:
1. a warrior, combatant , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. π. ἵππος a war-horse, charger , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8843.definition:
1. to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass. to be besieged, in a state of siege , (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander, to be dammed back , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. metaphorically to be besieged, pestered , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8844.definition:
1. a besieging, siege , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8845.definition:
1. gray, grizzled, grisly , of wolves, of iron, of the sea, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. mostly of hair, gray  or hoary  from age, (Homer); πολιοί gray-haired men , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;absolute, αἱ πολιαί (i.e. τρίχες); (Pindar); ἅμα ταῖς πολιαῖς κατιούσαις as the gray hairs  come down (i.e. from the temples to the beard), (Aristophanes Comicus); π. δάκρυον ἐμβαλών an old man's  tear, (Euripides) 
3. metaphorically hoary, venerable , (Euripides) 
4. like λευκός, bright, clear, serene , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8847.definition:
1. one of many , Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least , (Thucydides), etc.:—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8856.definition:
1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms , (Theognis Elegiacus) 
2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate , [Refs 5th c.BC, 5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8860.definition:
1. long-existing, of olden time, ancient , (Homeric Hymns) 
2. lasting for long , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;comparative -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8861.definition: to be very careful , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8862.definition:
1. in early Greek only as Dep. 
2. absolute to work hard, do work, suffer toil , (Homer); περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο were busied  about their supper, (Iliad by Homer); so, πεπόνητο καθ᾽ ἵππους was busy  with the horses, of a charioteer, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. metaphorically to be in distress, to distress oneself , (Iliad by Homer):—; to suffer, be sick , (Thucydides) 
4. with accusative to work hard at, to make  or do with pains  or care , (Homer) 
5. after (Homer), the active form prevails 
6. intransitive to toil, labour , (Theognis Elegiacus), attic; μάτην π. to labour  in vain, (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative, τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει do  not labour at things that profit not, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. with accusative cognate, π. πόνον, μόχθους to go through, suffer  them, [variant datesTragica Adespota; also with accusative partis, πονεῖν τὰ σκέλη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
8. absolute to labour, be hard-pressed, suffer , (Thucydides): to be worn out, spoilt , (Demosthenes Orator) 
9. Pass., impersonal, οὐκ ἄλλως αὐτοῖς πεπόνηται = πεπονήκασι, (Plato Philosophus) 
10. transitive, 
11. with accusative pers. to afflict, distress , (Pindar):—;Pass. to be worn out, to suffer greatly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
12. Pass., also, to be trained  or educated , (Aristotle Philosopher)
